financials_interim.notes: Company (standalone parent-entity) basis. Loss of Rs.(84,437)k vs Rs.(82,300)k prior year, broadly flat -- EPS -0.18 = -84,437/336,290,010 confirmed vs printed (0.18)/(0.24). short_term_borrowings = bank overdrafts and other short-term borrowings only (231,491); long_term_borrowings = 0 (Company had no interest-bearing bank liabilities, current or non-current, at 30.06.2026 -- 'Interest-bearing liabilities - banks' current line reads nil vs 248,825 a year earlier). cash_from_financing = 0 (no financing cash flow line items printed for the Company column this period). capex = acquisition of PPE (10,055); Company had no separate intangible asset acquisition line.

Group basis. Loss-making quarter -- Group swung to a Rs.(1,519,642)k net loss from a Rs.(544,187)k loss a year earlier, driven mainly by the South Asian and Middle East sector (segmental note pg.10: PBT loss widened to Rs.(1,175,124)k from Rs.(205,059)k). Revenue = 'Revenue' line (9,036,375) pre revenue-taxes, matching segmental note total (9,036,375) exactly -- net_revenue after revenue taxes (8,682,033) not used since 'Revenue' is the field most other entries in this DB use. operating_profit = 'Profit/(loss) from operations' line (-508,630), a loss (finance costs pushed it further into loss before tax). EPS -2.89 = -972,302 (profit attributable to equity holders) / 336,290,010 ordinary shares -- confirmed against printed 'Loss per share ... (2.89)'. short_term_borrowings = interest-bearing liabilities-banks current (4,088,366) + bank overdrafts and other short term borrowings (5,941,811) = 10,030,177; long_term_borrowings = interest-bearing liabilities-banks non-current only (24,914,389) -- interest-bearing lease liabilities (current 1,132,699 + non-current 21,871,117) are excluded from both borrowings fields since they're a separately labelled line in the filing (mostly hotel property leases, not bank debt). capex = acquisition of PPE (352,531) + acquisition of intangible assets (26,977) = 379,508 (both real capitalised outflows per the cash flow statement, pg.8-9). Seasonality note (pg.11): 'Two months of the period under review relates to the off season of the tourism industry both in Sri Lanka and other countries in which the Group operates' -- relevant context for a loss quarter. No occupancy rate / average room rate by property is disclosed anywhere in this filing -- genuine gap (see gaps_note in interim_updates). Do not confuse with SPEN (Aitken Spence PLC, the parent) -- this is the hotels subsidiary only.

interim_updates.note_text: Aitken Spence Hotel Holdings PLC (AHUN) reported Group revenue of Rs.9,036.4mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), down 12.2% YoY from Rs.10,294.7mn, as the quarter fell mostly in the industry's off-season (per the filing's own seasonality note, two of the three months covered 'relate to the off season of the tourism industry both in Sri Lanka and other countries in which the Group operates'). By segment (pg.10 note), the South Asian and Middle East sector -- AHUN's overseas resort portfolio -- drove the deterioration: its PBT loss widened to Rs.(1,175,124)k from Rs.(205,059)k a year earlier, while the Sri Lanka Resorts and Hotels sub-segment actually narrowed its loss slightly to Rs.(33,584)k from Rs.(38,931)k. The Group swung from an operating profit of Rs.404.1mn to an operating loss of Rs.(508.6)mn, and net finance expense rose 14.9% YoY to Rs.813.8mn (finance costs up 18.7% to Rs.980.1mn on higher net interest-bearing debt following new right-of-use lease additions -- ROU assets rose from Rs.12,729.9mn to Rs.25,315.3mn YoY). The Group loss attributable to equity holders widened to Rs.(972.3)mn from Rs.(351.1)mn, taking loss per share to Rs.(2.89) from Rs.(1.04). Foreign currency translation gains of Rs.2,353.7mn (largely from revaluing the overseas hotel portfolio) pushed total comprehensive income positive at Rs.519.7mn despite the trading loss, but this is a currency-translation effect on non-current assets, not operating cash profit.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for AHUN in this database, so no prior quarter (e.g. Q4 FY2025/26, quarter ended 31 March 2026) is available for a sequential comparison -- only the filing's own YoY comparative column is used. Genuine disclosure gap: no occupancy rate, average room rate (ARR), or RevPAR by property/region is disclosed anywhere in this interim filing (unlike some hotel-sector interims) -- the segmental note gives only revenue and PBT by sector (Sri Lanka vs South Asia & Middle East), not operational hotel KPIs, so the specific occupancy/rate drivers behind the overseas sector's widening loss cannot be quantified from this filing alone.
interim_updates.takeaway: The quarter's headline loss is concentrated in the South Asian and Middle East sector (overseas resorts), whose PBT loss more than quintupled YoY to Rs.(1,175.1)mn from Rs.(205.1)mn, against a Sri Lanka hotels segment that actually narrowed its own loss slightly -- so this is not a broad-based deterioration across the whole portfolio. Rising finance costs (net finance expense +14.9% YoY to Rs.813.8mn) on the back of a near-doubling of right-of-use lease liabilities are compounding the trading weakness. The Q1 quarter is structurally the group's seasonal trough (per its own disclosure), so the scale of the loss should be read against that seasonal base, not annualised.
operational_highlights: Group revenue down 12.2% YoY to Rs.9,036.4mn (from Rs.10,294.7mn), against a seasonally weak quarter -- 'two months of the period under review relates to the off season of the tourism industry both in Sri Lanka and other countries in which the Group operates' (note 5, pg.11)
South Asian and Middle East sector PBT loss widened to Rs.(1,175.1)mn from Rs.(205.1)mn a year earlier -- the dominant driver of the Group's swing to loss (segmental note, pg.10)
Sri Lanka Resorts and Hotels sub-segment loss narrowed to Rs.(33.6)mn from Rs.(38.9)mn -- the domestic hotel portfolio held up better than the overseas book this quarter
Group swung from an operating profit of Rs.404.1mn to an operating loss of Rs.(508.6)mn
Net finance expense up 14.9% YoY to Rs.813.8mn as right-of-use lease assets nearly doubled YoY (Rs.12,729.9mn to Rs.25,315.3mn)

Rs.2,353.7mn foreign currency translation gain (mainly revaluation of the overseas hotel book) pushed total comprehensive income to a positive Rs.519.7mn despite the trading loss -- a translation effect, not operating cash profit
Group loss attributable to equity holders widened to Rs.(972.3)mn from Rs.(351.1)mn; loss per share Rs.(2.89) vs Rs.(1.04)
key_drivers: South Asian and Middle East sector (overseas resorts) PBT loss widened over five-fold YoY to Rs.(1,175.1)mn from Rs.(205.1)mn -- the single largest driver of the Group's swing into a larger loss, per the segmental note (pg.10)

Net finance expense rose 14.9% YoY to Rs.813.8mn (finance costs +18.7% to Rs.980.1mn), driven by a near-doubling of right-of-use lease liabilities (Rs.9,917.4mn to Rs.21,871.1mn non-current lease liabilities YoY) -- a structural cost increase layered on top of the trading weakness

Seasonality: per the filing's own disclosure, two of the three months in this quarter fall in the tourism off-season across the Group's Sri Lankan and overseas markets -- this is structurally the Group's weakest quarter of the financial year
